ab_right.blurb: Right is a small sport crag in the Bow Valley, on the Upper Deck tier of the Cloud Break zone above Canmore. Five bolted lines all sit in the 5.12 range, so this is a spot for strong sport climbers, not for warming up. The climbing goes up streaked, bulging wall, and the setting is airy and exposed. Getting here means leaving the main trail and scrambling a short stretch of fourth-class ground to reach a broad shelf below the right end of the cable. Expect a committed approach and a high perch with big views.

ab_teen_titans_boulder.blurb: Teen Titans is a single limestone boulder in the House sector at the northwest edge of Frank Slide, in the Crowsnest Pass. It holds five sit-start problems that run from V0 up to about V3, so it suits climbers who want an easy to moderate stop rather than a project. The problems are short, with positive edges, jugs and one sidepull-heavy line that climbs harder than it looks, and one side of the block faces the highway. It is a handy add-on when working through the nearby House and Cartel boulders.

ab_trailside.blurb: Trailside is the first rock you meet on the walk along the shore of Lake Louise, the opening section of the Back of the Lake quartzite cliffs in Banff National Park. Five routes, four of them sport and one a crack climb on gear, run from 5.10 into the low 5.12s. The lines are steep and fingery, with a few crack lines mixed in. Because the wall rises right beside the busy tourist path, expect an audience of passersby while you climb. Sun and shade details are not well documented.

ab_bear_spirit.blurb: Bear Spirit is an ice and mixed crag in the Mt. Cory area of Banff National Park, reached from the Bow Valley Parkway. It has five lines: a couple of water ice pillars around WI3 to WI4 and three mixed lines in the M6 to M7 range. The broad bowl is popular for top-roping, which makes the pillars a common objective. The way in follows a creek bed and then goes up a roughly 10 m ice step, which catches out inexperienced parties, so bring crampons and treat the step seriously. An avalanche path can cross the creek-side trail.

ab_swamp_buttress.blurb: Swamp Buttress is a compact limestone sport crag in the Grassi Lakes area above Canmore. It has five bolted routes, mostly around 5.10, with one 5.11 and one 5.12 at the top end. The routes are short and stiff, with the wall in shade much of the time, so it can be a cool option in warm weather. Find it along the main Grassi trail just past the Rectory, then around the corner; one route is on a boulder beside the path. The wider Grassi Lakes cliffs are known for steep, pocketed rock.

ab_blackheart.blurb: Blackheart is a treed sport wall in Heart Creek, about 15 km east of Canmore in the Bow Valley. Five routes sit between 5.9 and 5.10, with most at 5.10, making it a friendly pick for climbers moving up from easier grades. A large dark corner high on the rock helps you spot the right wall. Most routes begin from a ledge reached by stepping off the interpretive trail and cutting a few metres into the trees. Heart Creek is mainly a summer destination and can fill up on weekends.

ab_the_solstice.blurb: The Solstice is a quiet little sport crag at Heart Creek in the Bow Valley, tucked among trees across the creek from First Rock. It carries five bolted routes with a wide spread, from about 5.5 up to 5.10, so beginners and intermediate climbers can both find something. To reach it, go to the Heart and Sole wall and follow a trail up and right for about three minutes to a prominent bolted face. The setting is more secluded than the busier walls along the interpretive trail. Heart Creek itself is mostly a summer area.
